messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up on the keyed-override idea from the kernel-selection RFC — proposal below. Goal: lightweight per-model + per-customer override that can force a fallback kernel for emergencies or experiments. Want opinions on priority, telemetry, TTLs, and rollout controls.

Jaya: +1. Do we treat these as "hard" overrides (force kernel) or hint-only (router may still choose)? Need both modes.

Morgan: I think we need 2 modes: `force` and `suggest`. Force should short-circuit routing and set kernel_used explicitly. Suggest should be best-effort but allow autoscaler/latency heuristics to override. Priority ordering: customer-specific > model-specific > route > global.

Tomas: Sketch of the override payload we can store in the control plane:
```
{
  "override_key": "cust:1234:model:neox-20b",
  "mode": "force",        // force | suggest
  "fallback_kernel": "int8-latency-optim",
  "owner": "oncall/team-ml",
  "reason": "safety_review",
  "expires_at": "2026-04-12T18:00:00Z"
}
```
This keeps it simple and extensible.

Nora: Telemetry requirements: every request should tag `override.key` (if present), `override.mode`, `kernel_selected`, and `decision_path` (e.g. "forced-by-override" vs "router-default"). Add a Prometheus counter `runtime_override_applied_total` with labels `(kernel, mode, owner, team)` and a trace annotation `override_applied=true`. We need these for quick rollbacks.

Infra-Bot: deploy:created automated note — feature flag `runtime.keyed_override` created (default: off). Use `/flag set runtime.keyed_override=true --env prod --note "enable keyed overrides for INCIDENT-4321"` to toggle.

Alex: Operational controls: plan to gate this behind 1) a feature flag, 2) RBAC for creating `force` overrides, 3) canary rollout (1% traffic first). Also automated safety checks: if enabling a `force` override causes median latency increase > 20% or error rate jump > 0.5% within 10m, we automatically unset and page oncall.

Jaya: Runbook needed. Short steps: detect override effect -> disable override via `/flag` -> run quick rollback -> escalate if persists. Can we add an API to simulate override effect on a small set of requests? :thinking_face:

Morgan: For rollout metrics, sample traces for 2% of requests and tag original route kernel + override kernel to compute distribution. Retain override logs for 90 days; shorter retention for ephemeral debug keys (24h).

Tomas: Default TTL proposal: 24h for ad-hoc emergency overrides, 7d for scheduled experiments, and indefinite only if `owner` is an enterprise customer with a signed agreement. Always require `owner` and `reason`.

Nora: Also add an audit log stream (immutable) that records who created/modified override, timestamps, and the control-plane version that applied it. Expose a small UI in Console to view active overrides and reason.

Alex: I'll update the RFC tracker with decisions and an action list: implement control-plane schema, add telemetry labels + counters, create RBAC checks, implement auto-unset watchdog, and a tiny Console panel. Link: https://go.redwood/repo/rfcs/kernel-override-followup (will post final). Planning a 1-week spike for infra + runtime changes.

Infra-Bot: infra: added flag rollout job — canary=1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks. Use `/flag roll runtime.keyed_override --strategy canary --steps 1,5,25,100`

Jaya: Sounds good. Can we include a quick checklist for the spike? 1) control-plane schema + migration 2) routing check in runtime 3) telemetry + dashboards 4) RBAC + runbook 5) Console view.

Morgan: I'll take telemetry + dashboard, Tomas will own runtime routing changes, Jaya will draft runbook, Alex will coordinate control-plane and RFC doc.

Alex: Thanks — appreciate the quick sync. Will post progress updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
